title: Charlie Parker
summary: Ben Webster told him about Parker, imitation drove Bird into drugs, and Rowles worked with him.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Lester had come in there to New York and he scared those guys just like Charlie Parker did! Ben Webster came back down... He heard about Charlie Parker and he went up to hear him, and he came back down to Birdland [sic] and he says, "Have you guys heard this Charlie Parker?" Now, he told me this himself. He says, "Well, you better get up there and listen to that. If you don't do that, you haven't lived. Wait'll you hear 'Cherokee.'" He says, "Holy God, there isn't anything on earth like that."

First thing you know, everybody in the town was playing Charlie Parker's style. And that's the reason why Charlie Parker went into dope heavy. Because every time he turned around and went into a club, he heard himself. Everybody was playing like Charlie Parker. They were all imitating. Sonny Stitt had him down, Jackie McLean was after his ass. Everybody was after the Bird. And the Bird was the Bird. And the Bird was a real nice guy!
I worked with him, and I took a trip with him, and I loaned him a white shirt with gun cufflinks. He brought them back to me. And he used to stand in the wings, and
he'd say, [RASPY] "Jimmy Rowles, 'There Will Never Be Another You' in B-flat. And he'd walk out and he'd start... I got along with him good.
I was very-very-very sad when I heard that he passed away. He passed away laughing, you know.
